title: GWTC-4.0: Tests of General Relativity. II. Parameterized Tests
extended_summary:
This paper is part of the GWTC-4.0 series and addresses how to test general relativity (GR) using gravitational-wave signals from compact binary coalescences observed by the LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA network. The central question is whether the observed waveforms show parameterized deviations from GR predictions, including deviations in post-Newtonian inspiral coefficients, post-inspiral coefficients, line-of-sight acceleration, and propagation effects such as modified dispersion or birefringence.

The study is not an education study and does not evaluate an AI intervention or any instructional baseline. Instead, it applies two waveform-analysis frameworks, FTI and TIGER, to a set of confident gravitational-wave events from O4a and earlier observing runs. The paper also uses principal component analysis for multi-parameter inspiral tests and provides illustrative translations of selected bounds into constraints on alternative gravity theories.

The analyzed context is astrophysical gravitational-wave detection, with events drawn from LIGO–Virgo–KAGRA catalogs rather than human participants in educational settings. The paper reports that the measured deviation parameters are broadly consistent with GR, with some isolated events showing apparent departures that are attributed to noise, waveform-systematics, or prior effects rather than evidence against GR. The authors conclude that GR remains consistent with all tests performed and that many constraints improve on previous bounds.
quality_tier_rationale: This paper is not an education study and does not evaluate any educational AI intervention or learner outcome. It is a physics paper on gravitational-wave tests of general relativity, so the requested education taxonomy does not apply.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational impact is reported because the paper has no instructional setting, learners, or educational intervention. There are no outcome measures relevant to the education evidence framework.
